messages.content:
You are the duty assistant of a data-centre facility team during the first hour of an event. You apply one approved intelligence pill and nothing else.

You see only what the team knew in the first hour ("signals"). You do not know how the event ended.

Rules:
1. Every action you recommend must come from a rule in the pill; give that rule's id. Do not invent actions or numbers.
2. Classify: "recurring" if the signals clearly meet the "when" conditions of one or more rules; "partly_recurring" if some rules apply but the signals also show something no rule addresses; "novel" if no rule applies.
3. Anything that matters but no rule covers goes into "not_covered", and then escalate.
4. Follow the guardrails.
5. Order next_actions by urgency.

Reply with JSON only:
{"classification":"recurring|partly_recurring|novel","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-001","because":"...","signals":["<id copied from signals>"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"...","rule_id":"R-001"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"...","reason":"..."},"not_covered":["..."]}

{"site":"South Central US region, one datacenter (San Antonio area, Texas)","signals":[{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S7","t_plus_min":0,"text":"At 08:42 UTC, lightning caused electrical activity on the utility supply, which caused significant voltage swells."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S8","t_plus_min":0,"text":"These swells triggered a portion of one Azure datacenter to transfer from utility power to generator power."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S9","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Additionally, these power swells shutdown the datacenter’s mechanical cooling systems despite having surge suppressors in place."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S10","t_plus_min":0,"text":"Initially, the datacenter was able to maintain its operational temperatures through a load dependent thermal buffer that was designed within the cooling system."},{"id":"AZ-SCUS-2018:S25","t_plus_min":47,"text":"Customer impact began at approximately 09:29 UTC when storage servers in the datacenter began shutting down as a result of unsafe temperatures."}],"pill":{"pill":"dc-cooling-loss@1.2.0","scope":{"assets":["data halls cooled by chilled-water plant (chillers, pumps, chilled-water loop)","utility and generator power feeding that plant"],"not_for":["IT service recovery and failover","fire suppression and life safety (follow the site emergency plan)"]},"rules":[{"id":"R-001","title":"Treat utility voltage swells as a cooling-plant threat, not just a power-transfer event","when":["storms are active in the area and the utility feed shows voltage sags or swells","a portion of the datacenter has transferred from utility power to generator power"],"then":["immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them","if mechanical cooling has shut down, treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion","transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active"],"why":"Voltage swells triggered a transfer to generator power and also shut down the mechanical cooling systems despite surge suppressors being in place; the site initially survived only on a load-dependent thermal buffer.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area"}},{"id":"R-002","title":"Act on thermal buffer depletion before automated shutdowns begin","when":["mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer","datacenter temperature is approaching safe operational thresholds"],"then":["treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted","expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin","recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down"],"why":"Once the thermal buffer was depleted the datacenter exceeded safe operational thresholds and automated shutdown began, but temperatures rose so quickly in places that some hardware was damaged before it could shut down.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started"}},{"id":"R-003","title":"Treat a control-system failover as a cooling-availability event, not a routine maintenance action","when":["the datacenter control system is in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts","the control system is exchanging state information with other control systems and with cooling equipment and temperature sensors"],"then":["treat the failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability and watch the cooling plant directly, not only the control system","expect that a fault in the control system logic during this exchange can make the control system unresponsive","verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback rather than assuming the fallback engaged"],"why":"The control system was mid-failover when a bug in third-party control logic caused excessive interactions with datacenter devices and left the control system unresponsive; the designed fallback to maximum cooling did not engage everywhere.","escalate":{"to":"facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer","trigger":"control system failover in progress or control system confirmed unresponsive"}},{"id":"R-004","title":"When the control system is down, work the cooling chain by hand and reset the PLCs","when":["the datacenter control system is unavailable and operators have minimum visibility into cooling health and state","cooling has not transitioned to maximum cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter"],"then":["do not wait for the control system to come back; manually investigate the affected cooling equipment","check the Programmable Logic Controllers controlling the air handling units, since they can be unresponsive even when the control system is the visible failure","reset the affected equipment and PLCs and place them into a maximum cooling configuration","confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down"],"why":"The control system was unavailable, purge failed, and recovery required manually investigating and resetting all affected equipment into maximum cooling; the unresponsive PLCs controlling some air handling units were what prevented both default cooling and purge from working.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures are rising and servers have begun powering off"}},{"id":"R-005","title":"Treat simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems as a single-point-of-failure event","when":["multiple cooling systems that are supposed to be redundant have failed at the same time","outside temperatures are extraordinarily high"],"then":["do not assume that remaining cooling capacity is sufficient; treat the data center as unable to maintain a safe operating temperature","immediately assess whether the data center can maintain a safe operating temperature","if not, plan to power down servers to prevent an even longer outage or damage to machines"],"why":"The review states that one data center could not maintain a safe operating temperature due to a simultaneous failure of multiple, redundant cooling systems combined with extraordinarily high outside temperatures, and that powering down was done to prevent an even longer outage or damage.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"simultaneous failure of redundant cooling systems and rising temperatures"}},{"id":"R-006","title":"Use progressive thermal load reduction before full shutdown","when":["data center temperatures are increasing and cooling capacity is insufficient","the data center is at risk of exceeding safe operating temperatures"],"then":["progressively decrease the thermal load within the data center space","consider terminating non-critical workloads such as Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover activities","if thermal load reduction is insufficient, power down servers to prevent an even longer outage and further impact to infrastructure"],"why":"The review describes terminating 42% of Preemptible VMs to reduce thermal load and ensure space for zonal failover, and later powering down servers to prevent a longer outage; it also commits to investigating more advanced methods to progressively decrease thermal load to reduce the probability of full shutdown.","escalate":{"to":"incident commander","trigger":"temperatures continue to rise despite initial load reduction"}}],"guardrails":[{"id":"G-001","text":"Do not rely on surge suppressors alone to keep mechanical cooling available during utility voltage swells; the review records that cooling shut down despite surge suppressors being in place."},{"id":"G-002","text":"Do not assume onsite redundancies make customer workloads safe from a datacenter cooling failure; the review states there are scenarios in which a cooling failure can impact customer workloads in the affected datacenter."},{"id":"G-003","text":"Do not treat purge mode as a guaranteed independent fallback while PLCs may be unresponsive; the review records that purge failed in the affected areas because the PLC controllers were unresponsive, and that purge is only being modified to bypass PLCs in newer designs."},{"id":"G-004","text":"Do not rely on the datacenter control system for visibility into cooling health during a control-system failure; the review records that the operations team had minimum visibility into cooling health and state while the control system was unavailable."},{"id":"G-005","text":"Do not assume the control-system failover mode that triggered this bug is available; the review records that this failover mode has been disabled in the interim to prevent recurrence."},{"id":"G-006","text":"Do not assume that redundant cooling systems provide protection against simultaneous failure, especially during extraordinarily high outside temperatures; the review records that multiple redundant cooling systems failed simultaneously and the data center could not maintain a safe operating temperature."}]}}
